name: add_episode
description:
Write text to the graph — graphiti extracts entities/edges, cogram annotates async. Returns task_id (~3s); pipeline runs ~15s in background.

    When:
      - User states a new fact, decision, preference, or context worth remembering.
      - User says "remember that..." / "don't forget..." (use extract_intent=True).
      - User states a commitment, choice, or recurring rule.
    Skip when:
      - Acknowledgments, greetings, thanks ("ok", "got it", "thanks").
      - Pure questions with no statement of fact.
      - You literally just wrote the same content earlier in this session.
      - Generic chitchat with no recall value.
    Inputs:
      - content: any text (e.g. "Siva prefers Postgres over MongoDB").
      - source_description: provenance tag (default "claude-mcp").
      - group_id: short label from list_groups (e.g. "default", "work").
      - extract_intent: False (default) runs the cheap path and may return `intent_suggestion`; True bills the team's intent_extractions cap and extracts decisions/preferences/cognitive patterns. Opt in for decisions, commitments, stated preferences, factual statements about the user, or explicit memory instructions.
    Pair with:
      - list_groups first if you don't know the group_id.
      - get_episode_task(task_id, wait_seconds=20) BEFORE reading the graph — avoids stale reads while the async pipeline finishes.
      - get_episode(uuid) to fetch the EPISODIC uuid (NOT the `episode_name` slug) before retract.

name: record_fact
description:
SPO wrapper around add_episode. Constructs '{subject} {predicate} {object}' and writes — locks edge structure better than free prose.

    When:
      - User states a clean structural fact ("Siva builds cogram", "cogram uses Neo4j").
      - You want a single deterministic edge instead of letting the extractor guess from prose.
    Skip when:
      - Content is narrative or multi-clause — use add_episode instead.
      - The same triple was already written earlier this session.
      - It's a question, acknowledgment, or hedged statement (not a confident fact).
    Inputs:
      - subject: entity name (e.g. "Siva").
      - predicate: relation; snake_case auto-converts to spaces ("name_is" -> "name is").
      - object: target entity or value (e.g. "Postgres").
      - group_id: short label from list_groups (e.g. "default").
      - extract_intent: same semantics as add_episode — False is the cheap path, True bills the intent cap.
    Pair with:
      - list_groups first if group_id is unknown.
      - get_episode_task(task_id, wait_seconds=20) BEFORE reading the graph — same async pipeline as add_episode.

name: retract
description:
Mark fact(s) as no-longer-believed. Filtered from search_graph; kept on disk for audit; bumps cache version so narratives re-generate on next read.

    **By default, name-based retract is team-wide.** If the same entity name exists in multiple groups (e.g. "Sarah Park" in both `candidates` and `internal_team`), retract affects ALL of them. Pass `group_id=X` to scope to one group. The server will surface a `warning` field in the response when a name-based retract spanned >1 group.

    `group_id` is ignored for uuid-based targets (edge uuid, episodic uuid) — those are naturally unique and don't need scoping.

    When:
      - User says "that's wrong", "I never said that", "delete that".
      - You catch an annotator hallucination or a stale fact contradicted by newer data.
      - User asks to forget a specific entity or episode.
    Skip when:
      - You only suspect a fact is wrong but haven't confirmed (read it first).
      - Target is the friendly `episode_name` "mcp_<ts>" — that's a slug, not a uuid.
      - User is correcting tone or wording, not the underlying belief — write a new episode instead.
    Inputs:
      - target: accepts (a) Entity name (substring), (b) edge uuid, or (c) EPISODIC uuid. NOT the `episode_name` slug from add_episode.
      - reason: optional free-text audit note (e.g. "user corrected on 2026-05-16").
      - group_id: OPTIONAL short label from list_groups. Scopes entity-name retraction to one group. Omit for team-wide retraction (you'll get a warning if it hit >1 group).
    Pair with:
      - get_entity_view(name, mode='edges') first to verify exactly what will be retracted.
      - get_episode(uuid) first if you're retracting by EPISODIC uuid — confirms the body.
      - list_groups when you want to scope but don't know the label.

name: search_graph
description:
Semantic search across the user's memory. Profile-aware on subjective queries ('would I...', 'how do I feel...'). Filters retracted edges automatically.

    **Default scope is EVERY group the user has data in.** Omit `group_id` unless you specifically want to scope to one bucket. Passing `group_id` restricts the search to that single bucket and hides everything else.

    When:
      - Fuzzy concept lookup ("find anything related to X").
      - You don't have an exact entity name, only a topic or phrase.
      - Subjective queries about the user ("how do I feel about...", "would I...").
    Skip when:
      - You already know the entity name — call get_entity_view(name) instead, it's cheaper and more direct.
      - You ran the same query in this session and the graph hasn't changed.
      - You need cross-decision pattern routing — use edges_by_pattern.
    Inputs:
      - query: any natural-language text (e.g. "candidate sourcing rules").
      - limit: max edges to return (default 10).
      - group_id: OPTIONAL short label from list_groups (e.g. "work", "candidates"). Omit to search ALL groups (recommended default). Pass a specific label only when you want to ignore everything outside that bucket.
    Pair with:
      - list_groups first if you genuinely want to scope to one group and don't know its label.
      - get_episode(uuid) to fetch the full body of an interesting hit.
      - get_entity_view(name, mode='edges') once a known entity name surfaces.
      - get_director_profile(group_id) when the query is subjective and you want one group's reasoning model.

name: whoami
description:
Return the bearer's identity: team_id + team name, project_id + project name, member_id, role, scopes.

    Use ONCE at the start of a session to confirm which account + which project + which permissions the current MCP connection has. Cheap (one parallel Supabase read for the human-readable names).

    When:
      - First call of a session if you (or the user) want to confirm "which Breeth account am I on?".
      - Debugging permission errors — `scopes` tells you exactly what the bearer can do.
      - Switching between multiple Breeth accounts and needing to verify which one is live.
    Skip when:
      - You already called whoami earlier this session and nothing about the connection has changed.
    Returns:
      - team_id / team_name: which organization this MCP is bound to
      - project_id / project_name: which project within that team
      - member_id: the account row id (for audit correlation)
      - role: 'admin' | 'manager' | 'member'
      - scopes: array of granted capabilities ('read' always implicit, 'write' / 'admin' explicit)

name: list_groups
description:
**First call of any session.** Returns each group_id with episode/entity/pattern/knot counts so you know what contexts exist before searching. Paginated. Scoped to the caller's team — solo individuals see their own lane; team members see shared + their individual lane; admins see everything in the team.

    Groups are short labels like "default", "work", "personal" — NOT the full t_xxx_g_xxx form. If you call this and pass the result into search_graph, you can pass the short label as-is.

    When:
      - First call of a session — discovers which contexts exist.
      - Before ANY group-scoped call (search_graph, get_director_profile, edges_by_pattern) when group_id is unknown.
    Skip when:
      - You already called list_groups earlier in this session — cache the result, don't re-list every turn.
      - You already know the group_id (e.g. user said "save to work").
    Inputs:
      - query: case-insensitive substring filter (e.g. "work").
      - limit: max groups to return (cap 200, default 20).
      - offset: pagination cursor.
    Pair with:
      - get_director_profile(group_id=X) to get the meta-narrative before searching.
      - search_graph(query, group_id=X) once you've picked a group.

name: list_cognitive_patterns
description:
Discover distinct cognitive_pattern labels with edge counts. Sorted most-reinforced-first. Scoped to the caller's team.

    When:
      - You want to know what thinking styles / recurring patterns exist before drilling into one.
      - Building a high-level map of the user's reasoning before making a recommendation.
    Skip when:
      - You already know the exact pattern name — call edges_by_pattern directly.
      - You called list_cognitive_patterns earlier this session — cache it.
      - You need raw edges or episodes — use search_graph or get_entity_view.
    Inputs:
      - query: substring filter (e.g. "legal", "hiring").
      - limit: max patterns (cap 200, default 20).
      - offset: pagination cursor.
    Pair with:
      - edges_by_pattern(pattern_name) for the actual reinforcing-edge evidence behind each pattern.
      - get_director_profile to see top patterns already ranked within a group.

name: edges_by_pattern
description:
**Cross-decision routing primitive.** Every edge whose cognitive_pattern matches, with intent_meta + director_vision intact. Substring match. Scoped to the caller's team.

    When:
      - About to make a constrained decision and want every prior decision under the same thinking style.
      - Turning "user rejected X once" into "user has a recurring rule".
      - Building a justified recommendation that cites past pattern instances.
    Skip when:
      - You don't know the pattern name yet — run list_cognitive_patterns first.
      - You want fuzzy semantic matching across all edges — use search_graph.
      - You only need a single entity's edges — use get_entity_view(name, mode='edges').
    Inputs:
      - pattern: substring of a cognitive_pattern label (see list_cognitive_patterns for exact names).
      - limit: max edges to return (default 25).
    Pair with:
      - list_cognitive_patterns first to discover exact names.
      - get_episode(uuid) on a surfaced edge's source_episode_uuid to inspect the raw context.

name: get_entity_view
description:
**Primary 'tell me about X' tool.** Three layers of view selectable via `mode`. Substring match on entity_name (up to 5 entities for narrative; up to `limit` edges/episodes). Scoped to the caller's team.

    When:
      - You have a known entity name (person, company, project) and want context.
      - mode='narrative' for compressed summary, 'edges' for raw provenance, 'episodes' for uuids needed before retract, 'all' for everything.
    Skip when:
      - You don't have an entity name yet — use search_graph for fuzzy lookup first.
      - You need pattern-level routing across many entities — use edges_by_pattern.
    Inputs:
      - entity_name: substring (e.g. "Siva", "Acme Corp").
      - mode: 'narrative' (default) | 'edges' | 'episodes' | 'all'.
      - limit: caps edges + episodes; narrative is always max 5 entities.
    Pair with:
      - search_graph beforehand if entity name is uncertain.
      - retract(target=uuid) using EPISODIC uuids surfaced by mode='episodes'.
      - get_episode(uuid) to read the full body of any surfaced episode.

name: get_episode
description:
Full content of one episode by uuid. Scoped to the caller's team.

    When:
      - Drilling into episode bodies after a uuid surfaced from get_entity_view, search_graph, or list_episode_tasks.
      - Confirming exactly what you're about to retract.
    Skip when:
      - You only have the friendly `episode_name` slug "mcp_<ts>" — that's NOT a uuid.
      - You want a list of episodes for an entity — use get_entity_view(name, mode='episodes').
      - You already inspected this episode in the current session.
    Inputs:
      - uuid: the EPISODIC uuid (not the `episode_name` slug that add_episode returns).
    Pair with:
      - get_entity_view(name, mode='episodes') to find uuids first.
      - retract(target=uuid) to roll back facts from this episode after confirming the body.

name: get_director_profile
description:
Compressed Director profile for ONE group: working-style summary + recurring visions + top cognitive patterns with reinforcing-edge examples. Scoped to the caller's team.

    When:
      - You picked a group_id (via list_groups or context) and want the user's reasoning model for it.
      - Need a single high-signal summary before searching or recommending.
      - Subjective query about the user within a specific group.
    Skip when:
      - You want the cross-group view — use get_unified_profile instead.
      - You only need raw edges or a single entity — use search_graph / get_entity_view.
      - You called it earlier this session for the same group_id.
    Inputs:
      - group_id: short label from list_groups (default "default").
      - top_patterns: how many cognitive patterns to include (default 10).
      - examples_per_pattern: reinforcing-edge examples per pattern (default 2).
    Pair with:
      - list_groups first if group_id is unknown.
      - edges_by_pattern(name) to drill into any surfaced pattern.
      - get_unified_profile for cross-group view.

name: get_unified_profile
description:
Director profile MERGED across every group_id with `appears_in_groups` per pattern. Scoped to the caller's team.

    When:
      - User has multiple groups and you want one "who is this person across all their work" answer.
      - Cross-context recommendation where group-specific framing would mislead.
    Skip when:
      - User has only one group — get_director_profile(group_id=X) is more focused.
      - You want group-scoped detail — use get_director_profile.
      - You already pulled the unified profile earlier in this session.
    Inputs:
      - top_patterns: how many merged patterns to include (default 15).
      - examples_per_pattern: reinforcing-edge examples per pattern (default 1). No group_id — merges all.
    Pair with:
      - list_groups to see what groups got merged.
      - get_director_profile(group_id=X) for any group you want in detail.
      - edges_by_pattern(name) to drill into a surfaced merged pattern.

name: list_episode_tasks
description:
List in-flight + recent background pipeline tasks (newest first). Process-local on cogram-core; cleared on its restart.

    When:
      - Introspecting whether earlier writes' annotations have settled.
      - Finding a task_id you lost track of.
      - Sanity-checking pipeline health (any 'failed' tasks in the last batch?).
    Skip when:
      - You already have the specific task_id — call get_episode_task directly.
      - You're not waiting on async settlement (most read paths don't need this).
    Inputs:
      - group_id: optional filter by group.
      - state: '' (all) | 'running' | 'done' | 'failed' | 'cancelled'.
      - limit: max tasks (default 50).
    Pair with:
      - get_episode_task(task_id, wait_seconds=N) to peek or block on a specific task.
      - cancel_episode_task(task_id) to abort a runaway task surfaced here.

name: get_episode_task
description:
Inspect or block on a background pipeline task. wait_seconds=0 peeks; wait_seconds=N blocks up to N seconds for terminal state. State ∈ running|done|failed|cancelled.

    When:
      - You just called add_episode/record_fact and need annotations settled before reading the graph (otherwise stale reads).
      - Verifying a specific task succeeded vs failed.
    Skip when:
      - You don't need the annotations to be settled before your next action (purely additive writes).
      - The task is already known-terminal from a prior call this session.
    Inputs:
      - task_id: returned by add_episode/record_fact in `cogram.task_id`.
      - wait_seconds: 0 peeks; N blocks up to N seconds for terminal state (default 0).
    Pair with:
      - list_episode_tasks to find lost task_ids.
      - cancel_episode_task to abort if the task is stuck or off-track.

name: cancel_episode_task
description:
Cooperatively cancel a still-running pipeline task. Already-written annotations stay; only future steps are skipped.

    When:
      - A task is stuck, took the wrong direction, or rate-limit chains will block other writes.
      - User retracted the source content and you want to stop downstream annotation.
    Skip when:
      - The task is already terminal (done/failed/cancelled) — cancel is a no-op.
      - You actually want the pipeline to finish — let it run; it's async.
    Inputs:
      - task_id: live task_id (returned by add_episode/record_fact or found via list_episode_tasks).
    Pair with:
      - list_episode_tasks(state='running') first to confirm the task is still live.
      - get_episode_task(task_id) afterward to confirm cancelled state.
